reason: No skill covers proving Postgres grant assertions (has_table_privilege matrices, seed re-grants, CI guards). The CX-01/DB-01 run showed the CI guard query only counts as a guard once an injected offender is named in a rolled-back transaction. Class-level lesson for any future audited table or grant change.

The DB-02 window tests were proven by mutation with a before/after function hash, and the vacuity check caught nothing only because the snapshot moved. Grants were restated after CREATE OR REPLACE. Both belong to the existing grant/privilege proof skill.

The draft-only events trigger protects 22 columns from a hand-written list. Without a test tied to live grants, a column granted later passes silently. The current_user rule decides which writers are refused, so each caller class needs its own check.

Episode showed the mutation catalogue passing two survivors (RPC survey check, RPC draft check) only because a trigger masked each layer; fixing it required dropping the masking layer and adding RPC-level tests. The PUBLIC EXECUTE default on the new RPC was found late (anon could execute update_event_with_blocks). Both are grant/guard-proof lessons this skill already governs.

DB-05 (audited roster edit) revoked table UPDATE from authenticated. Three lessons surfaced: (1) 42501 is raised by both the grant and a trigger, so tests must assert the message to prove the layer; (2) an UPDATE matching zero rows under RLS returns no error, so the test silently passes unless it asserts the row count and the probe has the JWT claims the SELECT policy needs; (3) a revoke breaks tests that proved triggers by writing as the role, and the posture matrix must move in the same change. Also a reusable mutant harness with fingerprint restore check.

This episode's DB-05 work showed three gaps the skill does not cover: a table grant left in place with no policy (DELETE answered 200 []), a seed whose blanket grant re-opened UPDATE/DELETE after the revoke, and a mutant (D18) that killed zero tests until a new test was added. The skill's grant rules do not name any of these.
The DML-verb rule misses MAINTAIN, a non-DML table privilege that the trace showed live on the anon role. A future revoke sweep following this skill would leave it open.
The DB-05 change revoked UPDATE and DELETE and had to re-assert the revoke in three separate artefacts. The skill names only the seed, so the replay gate and the matrix are easy to miss.
